notes: Weapon figures are the book's modifiers; null is the book's n/a. strength is the minimum Strength to use the weapon (a weapon's and a shield's are met separately); range is the range increment in paces. Every natural weapon uses Brawl; Strength, Load and Cost do not apply to them.

weapons.name: Dodge
weapons.description: Simply getting out of the way of opponents, without trying to do damage.

weapons.name: Fist
weapons.description: Any unarmed attack made with the hands.

weapons.name: Kick
weapons.description: Unarmed attacks made with the feet are more powerful, but less accurate. Characters may kick standing opponents, but most often this attack is used against prone enemies.

weapons.name: Gauntlet
weapons.description: A heavy glove of hardened leather or chain mail. It does more damage than a bare fist, and is more effective at blocking attacks. Full armor always includes gauntlets and partial armor sometimes does (troupe's option).

weapons.name: Bludgeon
weapons.description: A sap (a leather bag filled with lead shot) or any heavy object like a stone or a small hammer: any improvised bashing weapon such as a rock or hand tool.

weapons.name: Dagger
weapons.description: Any knife-like weapon between about 6 inches and 14 inches long. Daggers are commonly carried as tools, as well as for self-defense.

weapons.name: Knife
weapons.description: Any sharp knife of 6 inches or less. Knives are even more common than daggers; they are everyday tools.

weapons.name: Axe
weapons.description: A common woodcutter's axe or a heavier battle weapon, small enough to wield in one hand, albeit sometimes awkwardly.

weapons.name: Club
weapons.description: Simply a heavy stick, or an iron-shod weapon.

weapons.name: Hatchet
weapons.description: Any axe with a haft shorter than about 18 inches. It does less damage than a longer axe because of poor leverage. Some hatchets are suitable for throwing.

weapons.name: Lance
weapons.description: Used only from horseback, where it is a Single weapon. A dismounted rider may wield it two-handed as a Long Spear.

weapons.name: Mace
weapons.description: Any heavy, bludgeoning weapon with a weighted head, usually made of iron and usually spiked or flanged. Includes spiked clubs, military hammers and other one-handed bashing weapons.

weapons.name: Mace and Chain
weapons.description: One or more weighted, spiked or flanged heads connected to a haft by a length of stout chain. Sometimes called a "morning star."

weapons.name: Short Spear
weapons.description: A spear short enough to wield in one hand, from 4 to 7 feet in length. A very common battlefield weapon, often used by warriors who cannot afford a sword.

weapons.name: Short Sword
weapons.description: Any bladed weapon from 14 inches to about 28 inches long, single- or double-edged, usually with a sharp point for thrusting. Large woodsman's knives are big enough to count as short swords.

weapons.name: Long Sword
weapons.description: Any sword over 28 inches long, typically used by horsemen because it is long enough to reach opponents on foot. Long swords are typically straight, even in Arabia.

weapons.name: Buckler
weapons.description: A small shield that buckles to the forearm, usually made of metal. It is light enough that other objects can be held in the shield hand.

weapons.name: Round Shield
weapons.description: A wooden shield that is cheap and easy to make.

weapons.name: Heater Shield
weapons.description: Often made of a combination of wood and metal, this shield tapers to a point at the bottom. Its outer surface is convex, to better deflect blows.

weapons.name: Cudgel
weapons.description: A heavy, two-handed club.

weapons.name: Farm Implement
weapons.description: Rakes, scythes, mattocks and other farm implements used as improvised weapons: awkward, and apt to break under the rigors of combat.

weapons.name: Flail
weapons.description: A two-handed, heavier version of the common threshing flail: effective and easy to make. Treat a smaller, one-handed flail as a Mace and Chain.

weapons.name: Pole Arm
weapons.description: Bladed, long-handled weapons, from the continental guisarme to the English "brown bill": they vary in detail but share a long cutting blade, and the same statistics.

weapons.name: Pole Axe
weapons.description: Any axe too large to wield one-handed, typically four to six feet long.

weapons.name: Long Spear
weapons.description: Any spear too long to use one-handed, from about 8 to 15 feet or longer. Includes the lance, if used dismounted.

weapons.name: Great Sword
weapons.description: A heavy, two-handed sword, designed to penetrate heavy armor.

weapons.name: Staff
weapons.description: A common, inexpensive weapon often carried about the countryside for self-defense.

weapons.name: Warhammer
weapons.description: Includes other weighted, two-handed bludgeoning weapons, such as a two-handed mace.

weapons.name: Throwing Axe
weapons.description: Can be wielded in melee as a hatchet.

weapons.name: Javelin
weapons.description: Can be wielded in melee as a short spear.

weapons.name: Knife
weapons.description: A knife thrown rather than wielded.

weapons.name: Sling
weapons.description: Although the sling uses the Thrown Weapon skill, it has much greater range than a hand-hurled weapon. Requires two free hands to load and fire; its Load includes its ammunition.

weapons.name: Stone
weapons.description: A stone heavy enough to hurt someone, about the size of a fist.

weapons.name: Long Bow
weapons.description: The famous English longbow, which equally famously required years of training and physical conditioning to use. Requires two free hands to load and fire; its Load includes its arrows.

weapons.name: Short Bow
weapons.description: Weaker than the long bow, but still powerful enough to use on the battlefield or to hunt large game. Requires two free hands to load and fire; its Load includes its arrows.

weapons.name: Grapple
weapons.description: A grapple attack instead of a normal attack, against an opponent no larger than the creature's Size + 1 (the Grapple Quality). Also the creature's Defense against anyone outside the grapple.

weapons.name: Dodge
weapons.description: Simply getting out of the way of opponents, without trying to do damage.

armor.name: Quilted/Fur
armor.description: Quilted cloth, a thin layer of leather, or layers of leather-strap-wrapped fur or cloth: the most basic of armor. Partial only.

armor.name: Heavy Leather
armor.description: Very thick leather, or leather hardened by wax impregnation or baking: better at deflecting crushing damage. Partial only.

armor.name: Metal Reinforced Leather
armor.description: Leather reinforced with studs, rings, or other metal pieces, which strengthen it against slashes and cuts.

armor.name: Leather Scale
armor.description: Leather broken up into a flexible array of scales, which allows thicker pieces of leather.

armor.name: Metal Scale
armor.description: Small overlapping metal plates in place of leather scales: more protection while keeping flexibility, although metal weighs slightly more.

armor.name: Chain Mail
armor.description: A suit of flexible metal made of links of chain: the top of 1220 technology.
